title: The Acoustics Point South, Not to Losee (Claims)
description: An unnamed acoustics engineer reportedly places the shot South, above the Teachers' balcony. The site's own Canon audio analysis puts the rifle at ~120m — the Losee roof. Both cannot be right.

title: The ATF Fragment Shows Only Class Characteristics (Claims)
description: The ATF's Sept 17, 2025 lab report reportedly could neither identify nor exclude Robinson's Mauser 98 as the source of the recovered jacket fragment — a documented gap, widely overclaimed by both camps.

title: The Burnt Object as a RODE Transmitter (Claims)
description: Proponents read a melted audio jack and a warning symbol into a charred mass photographed in the SUV. The imagery cannot support the identification, and the theory cannot agree on the model.

title: The Canon XA55 Audio and a Stage Detonation (Claims)
description: An analysis of uncompressed Canon XA55 audio claims three low-frequency arrivals including a detonation at the tent. Reflections off campus buildings produce exactly the same pattern.

title: The Rick Cutler Hand-Device Claim (Claims)
description: Recorded only as a specimen of what is circulating. Anonymous accounts read a dark object in a named private citizen's hand as a trigger. This site does not advance the claim.

title: Electrocution as Trigger and Redundancy (Claims)
description: A strand of theory holds electricity was part of the mechanism. No agency reported any electrical injury, and electrical injury leaves pathology nobody has described. This is the weakest material on the site.

title: No Blood Spray, No Exit Wound (Claims)
description: The most-repeated suspicion: a .30-06 should have blown through the neck and sprayed blood. The counterargument includes a physics error that undercuts the analysts making it.

title: Is the Front Neck Wound an Entrance or an Exit? (Claims)
description: Proponents argue the front neck wound is an exit — and contradict each other completely about where the shot came from. None has produced medical documentation.

title: The Mic Placed Under, Not Over, the Shirt (Claims)
description: The RODE transmitter was reportedly worn under Kirk's shirt against his torso — the precondition every contact-device theory needs. Under-shirt placement is also routine professional practice.

title: The Snapped Necklace and the Residue Search (Claims)
description: Both camps treat the snapped chain as a clue. One cited expert says cavitation from a bullet explains it; another says a PETN charge in the pendant did. Both cannot be right.

title: Suspicious About Cause of Death
description: Twelve things citizen investigators find suspicious about the official rifle-shot account of how Charlie Kirk died — the energy mismatch, the shirt sequence, the acoustics, the ATF fragment. Attributed claims, not proven findings.

title: The Shot-Through-the-Heart Narrative (Claims)
description: A thesis that the earliest on-camera witnesses described a chest-and-heart wound because that is the wound a shaped charge was intended to produce — and that the charge tilted and struck the neck instead. The white shirt is what falsifies the heart description.

title: The Shirt and Necklace Move Before the Blood (Claims)
description: Analysts argue the shirt balloons and the chain snaps several frames before blood appears. Hydrostatic cavitation predicts exactly that, and 30fps cannot resolve a millisecond event.

title: Baron Coleman Says Robinson Is in Grave Danger (Claims)
description: Baron Coleman says he is 100% convinced Tyler Robinson was framed and is in grave danger of being killed. He offers no evidence of any threat, and Robinson is held in isolation. Attributed opinion.

title: Defense Acquiescence to the Sua Sponte Gag Order (Claims)
description: Critics ask why defense counsel never challenged Judge Tony Graf's own-motion publicity order. Trial-publicity orders in capital cases are routine and usually protect the defendant. Attributed claims only.

title: The Jailhouse Informant Transport Order (Claims)
description: A transport order for inmate Jaxson Thomas Fox is read as evidence of a jailhouse snitch being positioned. A transport order is a ministerial docket entry that reveals nothing about testimony.

title: Kent's Halted Probe as Defense Ammunition (Claims)

title: Five-Second Fragment - The Moment Itself
description: A five-second fragment framed on the tent that contains the final words spoken and the moment Charlie Kirk was struck, followed by an immediate pan away into the crowd.

title: Eleven-Minute Wide Angle - The Full Q&A
description: An eleven-minute elevated wide shot covering the last of the UVU question-and-answer session, the theological debate, the final exchange, and the shot itself.

title: Elevated Angle - Crowd Dispersal Across the Plaza
description: A 37-second elevated capture that starts on the tent, catches the reports, and then pulls back to show the whole UVU plaza emptying in every direction.

title: Seventy-Minute Livestream - Before, During and After
description: A 70-minute citizen livestream walking the UVU campus before the event, catching the shot off-camera, and then recording eyewitness accounts and the police response for nearly an hour afterwards.

title: News-Narrated Upscale of the Plaza Angle
description: A 29-second repackaging of the elevated plaza angle with an added synthetic news voiceover, filed in the archive with a note that the upscaling introduced artefacts.

title: Balcony Angle With Slow-Motion Replays (Music Added)
description: A 46-second re-edit of the balcony phone angle at UVU, running the moment of the shot and the crowd flight in real time and slow motion, with a music bed laid over the original audio.

title: Balcony Angle — Two Pops and the Crowd in Flight
description: A 37-second balcony phone capture at UVU: two sharp pops, the crowd dropping and scattering, and the filmer calling out that someone has been shot.

title: Twelve Minutes Before: Crowd, Arrival and the Sponsor Pitch
description: A 12-minute high-resolution walk through the UVU crowd before the event: chanting, Charlie Kirk arriving by black SUV, counter-protesters on the balcony, and a YRefy sponsor introduced as Lane.

title: Ground Level After the Shot — Alternate Audio Pass
description: A 115-second ground-level walk through the UVU plaza during and after the panic, from the balcony counter-protesters to scattered attendees; an alternate audio pass of the same footage with a differing transcript.

title: Ground Level After the Shot — Primary Audio Pass
description: The primary audio pass of a 115-second ground-level walk through the UVU plaza during and after the panic, showing the balcony group, the fleeing crowd, the SAVE AMERICA tent and discarded debris.

title: Eleven Seconds: The Last Question and the Report
description: An 11-second vertical capture of the final exchange at the UVU tent, ending at the instant of the report; the stored visual description of this clip appears to misread that instant as a tackle.

title: Counting or Not Counting Gang Violence — The Last Exchange
description: Fifteen seconds of vertical phone video from the crowd at UVU, ending on Charlie Kirk's last recorded words: Counting or not counting gang violence? The clip cuts immediately after.

title: Crowd Angle — The Last Question, Then the Scatter
description: Thirty-seven seconds of continuous handheld phone video: the last question, the report, and the crowd's scatter from the plaza into a parking structure. An archive-retrieved copy with no poster credit.

title: Ten Seconds — Fixed Frame on the Tent at the Report
sidebar_label: Ten Seconds — Fixed on the Tent
description: Ten seconds of vertical phone video from the back of the UVU crowd: a fixed frame on the tent through the last question, the report, and the camera dropping to the ground.

title: Handheld Capture, Shot to Parking Structure
description: The second archive copy of a 37-second handheld capture at UVU. Its stored visual description wrongly calls the footage a drill; this page corrects that and sets out what is and is not established.

title: The Chair That Buckled — Platform Hardware Close-Up
description: Seven seconds, with instant slow-motion replay, of a folding chair buckling under a seated speaker on an American Comeback platform. Kept for what it shows about the riser and seating hardware.

title: Ten Minutes to the Very End — The Full Final Q and A
sidebar_label: Ten Minutes to the Very End
description: The longest single angle in this section: ten minutes of the UVU Q and A, a nine-minute theology debate and then the final firearms-policy question, ending on Charlie Kirk's last recorded words.

title: 4K 60fps From the South: The Question, the Shot, the Exit
description: A 1:03 dual-angle 4K 60fps edit that runs from the final gang-violence question through the shot to the evacuation of Charlie Kirk into a waiting SUV.

title: Eight Seconds From the Walkway: Zoom, Two Reports, Panic
description: An 8-second student phone clip filmed from an elevated UVU walkway that zooms to the tent as a report sounds, whip-pans to the operator's own face, and catches the crowd breaking.

title: Under the Walkway: A Wide Shot That Ends in a Blur
description: A 10-second wide shot of the UVU tent from beneath the campus walkway, holding steady through the final question until the report at about six seconds sends the camera down.

title: Unverified Entry: Sidecars Describe a Different Recording
description: A 1:12:15 file filed as the full 4K UVU capture whose stored transcript and visual description both describe an unrelated Michigan legislative committee hearing. Flagged as unverified.

title: Six Seconds, Unwatermarked: The Crowd Before the Break
description: A 6-second unwatermarked variant of a crowd-level clip at the UVU Prove Me Wrong table, catching the gang-violence exchange and the crowd's reaction from behind.

title: Six Seconds, Watermarked: The Crowd Flinches
description: The watermarked 6-second variant of the crowd-level UVU clip, running from the gang-violence answer into the report at about three seconds and the crowd's flinch.

title: Nineteen Seconds: The Question and the Roar
description: A 19-second spectator clip of the final Prove Me Wrong exchange at UVU, ending on the crowd's reaction and stopping before the shot.

title: Thirty-Nine Seconds: Two Questions, Then the Hillside Drops
description: A 39-second clip that runs from the transgender-shooters question through the gang-violence answer to a report at about 25 seconds and hundreds of people going flat on the terraced lawn.

title: The Archive Variant: Same Thirty-Nine Seconds, Second Copy
description: A second 39-second copy of the same handheld clip, filed under an archive-suffixed filename, carrying the same exchange and the same report at about 25 seconds.

title: Camera Pointed Away: Protesters on the Balcony
description: A 45-second clip whose camera is aimed at counter-protesters on an elevated UVU walkway rather than at the tent, catching the final exchange on audio only before the frame breaks up.

title: Kirk Rifle Roof: The Fox News Airing of the Roof-Descent Video
description: A 38-second phone recording of a Fox News broadcast playing the released security video of a person descending from the Losee Center roof, over a law-enforcement briefing describing palm prints and Converse shoes.

title: Livestream From the Plaza: Q&A, the Shot, and 20 Minutes of Witnesses
description: A 30-minute citizen livestream that runs through the theology and gun-statistics Q&A, the shot itself, and roughly twenty minutes of on-the-spot eyewitness interviews during the evacuation.

title: GoPro: "Ring Radiates Upward" - A 27-Second Wide Shot
description: A 27-second static wide shot of the UVU tent, held because of a claimed upward-radiating ring artifact that neither the transcript nor the automated description of the file records.

title: Full Video From North: The Final Question and the Shot
description: A 39-second view from the north side capturing the last exchange about mass-shooting statistics, the shot at about 25 seconds, and the crowd going flat on the grass.

title: Full Shot Side: The Shot and the Run to the Minivan

description: A 37-second side-angle capture running from the last question through the shot at about eight seconds and on to the security team moving Kirk through the underpass into a black minivan.

title: Crowd Arrival Clip: A Public Figure Walking a Vehicle Line
sidebar_label: Crowd Arrival Clip at a Tour Event
description: This short video captures a public appearance by Donald Trump Jr. as he walks through a crowd of cheering supporters at an outdoor venue.

title: "I Turned the Camera Off Right Before the Gun Went Off"

title: Crowd Footage from IMG_2390, With Its Metadata Attached
description: This video features drone-like handheld footage of a large, energetic outdoor crowd of college students gathered for a political event on a campus plaza. The crowd is cheering, clapping, and recording with their phones around a tent marked "The American…

title: Nineteen Seconds of the Aftermath, Left Side of the Courtyard
description: A 19-second phone capture from the left of the UVU courtyard immediately after the shot: the crowd flat on the terraces, an empty stage, and a protective detail moving someone toward black SUVs.

title: Sixteen Minutes Inside the Crowd, Before the Shot
description: A 16-minute TikTok capture from inside the UVU audience covering the Q&A before the shooting: stage layout, crowd scale, camera rigs and security positions. The footage ends before the shot.

title: Split-Screen: The Stage and the Security Feed, Synchronised
description: A 1:55 third-party edit pairing hand-held stage footage with a campus security camera, tracking a dark-clothed figure across the lawn and parking lot. A proposed synchronisation, not a verified timestamp.

title: Relaying the SU-BTT Claim: Owens, Parker and a Failed Screen Recording
description: A 2:31 commentary clip reading out Candace Owens's Egyptian-jet timeline and pointing to Sam Parker's search-pattern work. A relay of others' claims with no documents shown on screen.

title: 'GARY 828': A Fourteen-Minute Video Essay on the Footage Record
sidebar_label: Video Essay on the Footage Record
description: An anonymous 14-minute analysis reel asking why so little clear footage exists despite multiple professional cameras, arguing against the trap-door theory, and speculating about people in frame. Speculation reported, not adopted.

title: Tim Ballard at the Garden Tomb: 'It Was Not a Lone Shooter'
description: A 24-second social clip in which Tim Ballard, filmed at the Garden Tomb in Jerusalem, tells viewers not to believe the official account. A statement of conviction with no evidence offered.

title: Filming When the Shot Was Fired: The Plaza From Above
sidebar_label: Filming When the Shot Was Fired
description: A continuous 59-second elevated capture of the UVU plaza that begins twelve seconds before the shot and keeps running, with the camera operator's contemporaneous 'one shot' remark on the audio track.

title: The Last Four Minutes, Uncut
description: Four continuous minutes of the UVU Q&A running from an exchange on the resurrection through the final question about mass shooters, ending on the word that lands just before the event stops.

title: Surveillance Clip of a Figure Carrying a Long Object
description: A silent 54-second surveillance compilation, stamped 9/10/2025 12:23:35 PM and carrying an FBI channel logo, following a figure in dark clothing across a UVU lawn.

title: Six Seconds From Inside the Building
description: A six-second pan through a glass wall above the UVU courtyard, showing the size of the crowd and a staffed table set up inside the building overlooking it.

title: Multi-Angle Grid of the Final Question
description: A 160-second multi-panel edit holding a fixed stage shot on top while a grid of crowd and crew angles cycles below, carrying the audio of the last question at the microphone.

title: The Plaza Empties: One Pop, Then Panic
description: A 59-second handheld pan across the packed UVU plaza that catches the sound at about 0:11 and then tracks the crowd scattering, with bystanders on the audio saying one shot was fired.

title: The Crowd Scatters Across the UVU Plaza (running1)
description: An 11-second anonymous phone capture, shot from above, of the crowd breaking and running across the UVU plaza. No speech is audible. One of two running clips held in the investigation archive.

title: View From Inside, Looking Out at the Crowd (roofshooter2)
sidebar_label: Inside looking out at the crowd
description: A six-second pan filmed through an interior window at UVU, showing the seated crowd on the grass slope and an indoor information table. Filed under the roof clips, but no rooftop figure is visible in frame.

title: It's a Gunshot, I Think — The Crowd Breaks (running2)
description: An 11-second phone capture from above the UVU courtyard as the crowd scatters. A bystander says on tape, Bro. It's a gunshot, I think — a rare recording of the moment being identified in real time.

title: Campus Surveillance Composite, 9/10/2025 (roofshooter3.ia)
description: A silent 1:40 composite of UVU security camera angles dated 9/10/2025, cutting between feeds to follow a figure in dark clothing across lawn, lot and roadway. An archive copy of the roofshooter3 clip.

title: The 70-Minute Livestream: Before, During and After the Shot
description: An independent streamer's unbroken 1:09:43 walk through UVU on 9/10/2025 — protester interviews before the event, the shot itself, then live eyewitness accounts of blood, sound, roof searches and absent screening.

title: Surveillance Cut Stamped 12:23:35 PM (roofshooter3)
description: The same silent 1:40 UVU security-camera composite as the archive copy, but this retrieval carries a legible burned-in timestamp reading 9/10/2025 12:23:35 PM — seconds after the shot.

title: There's Somebody On The Roof Right There (roofshooter1)
sidebar_label: Somebody on the roof right there
description: A 20-second phone clip in which two off-camera bystanders point out a figure on a rooftop and say he just ran in from over there. The same audio appears in a mapping clip published by Jason Cain.

title: The Bednarz UVU Original - Reference Capture
description: The eleven-minute unaltered Blake Bednarz capture of the UVU event, pinned to IPFS with a metadata report and forensic information sheet, and used as the reference original for the whole archive.

title: George Webb Ties Together DuPont, Burisma and the Flights
description: A 170-second handheld monologue in which George Webb strings together a claimed post-death phone call, a name from his older Burisma research, Egyptian flight counts and event-surveillance claims.

title: The Chain of Evil Map — A 13-Minute Walkthrough
description: A 13:33 screen-recorded walkthrough of the Chain of Evil diagram, mapping a hypothesised route from foreign intelligence methods through media, money and institutions down to citizens.

title: The 9:24 AM Camera Frame and the Question It Raises
description: A 27-second clip pairing courtroom testimony about a 9:24 AM campus arrival with a presenter asking which Turning Point USA representative was met that morning.

title: The Same Two Seconds, Six Times, From Six Angles
sidebar_label: The same two seconds, six times
description: A 55-second study that replays the instant of the shot from six framings, twice in slow motion, and ends on a card reading JUSTICEFORCHARLIEKIRK. The shirt movement is what the edit is built to show.

title: A Stage Rush, A Tackle, And A Red Arrow At The Ear
description: A 1:30 music-scored loop of a stage-rush being tackled at a Prove Me Wrong event, with one inserted still of a red arrow pointing at Charlie Kirk's ear. Filed as south-angle material it does not contain.

title: The Discord Logs Video: An Anonymous Source and a Substack Post
description: A 22-minute narrated read-through of a Substack post publishing Discord archives supplied by an anonymous person claiming to know Tyler Robinson and Lance Twiggs, with photographs of the apartment.

title: Baron Coleman: "Tyler Robinson Is in Grave Danger"
description: A 41-second clip in which attorney and radio host Baron Coleman states his conviction that Tyler Robinson was framed, was not meant to survive to surrender, and cannot be allowed to reach trial.

title: "There Was None" — The Body-Camera Answer On the Record
description: Thirty-five seconds of appeal-hearing audio in which a county representative states on the record that a search was made for body camera footage and none was found.

title: The Records Request, Read Into the Record
description: Fifty-eight seconds of appeal-hearing audio in which counsel for CBS News states the exact scope of the sheriff lobby video request and the county's stated grounds for denying it.

title: Why Does the Request Start at 6 p.m.? — Coleman on the Appeal
description: Baron Coleman plays the appeal-hearing audio and argues two points from it: that the denial implies the lobby footage exists, and that the request window opening at 6 p.m. is telling.

title: The Cowboy's Smokehouse Receipt, Filmed
description: Twelve silent seconds of a printed 9/10/25 restaurant receipt showing an 8:55 PM order and a 9:47 PM card payment. No person appears; the receipt is unauthenticated and the customer unidentified.

title: Baron Coleman On What An Early Surrender Time Would Mean
sidebar_label: Coleman On An Early Surrender Time
description: A 4:00 podcast clip in which Baron Coleman argues that if Tyler Robinson surrendered in the afternoon rather than after 9pm, the prosecution timeline collapses, and notes the missing surrender video.

title: Sheriff Brooksby Describes The 8:02 Phone Call From A Retired Friend
description: A 68-second press-conference clip in which Washington County Sheriff Nate Brooksby recounts the 8:02pm call from a retired colleague that began the surrender, and the family's role in arranging it.

title: Walking The Route: Doorbell Cameras To Three Wooded Areas
description: A 6:56 first-person walk-through retracing the route attributed to the suspect, from a doorbell camera north of campus to the roof and out to three candidate locations for the rifle.

title: Project Constitution: Doorbell Footage From The Morning Of September 10
description: A silent 4:59 cut of Wyze doorbell video time-stamped 2025-09-10 08:22, posted by Project Constitution and credited to a YouTube researcher, presented as showing a young man walking a suburban street hours before the UVU shooting.

title: Prosecutor Describes The Suspects Unusual Gait On Campus Surveillance
description: A 50-second press-conference clip in which a prosecutor narrates campus surveillance of the suspect entering UVU at about 11:51 a.m., describing a stiff right leg said to be consistent with a rifle concealed in his trouser leg.

title: Six-Second Pan Across The UVU Hall Of Flags Toward The Crowd
description: A silent six-second handheld pan shot from inside a UVU interior space with international flags overhead, sweeping across the outdoor crowd and a row of tabled staff. Filed under Tyler Robinson footage despite showing neither.

title: Wyze Porch Camera, Suburban Street, 08:22 On September 10
description: A silent 34-second Wyze porch-camera clip stamped 2025-09-10 08:22:50, reposted by Muppet Masher, showing a quiet suburban street, a passing sedan, a dog walker and a second pedestrian on the far sidewalk.

title: Governor Cox Says The Suspect Changed Clothes Twice On September 10
description: A 22-second press-conference clip in which Utah Governor Spencer Cox states the suspect wore different clothing when first spotted on campus, changed on the roof, and was later arrested in the clothing he had worn before the shooting.

title: Six Seconds Of A White Object Crossing The Sky Above The Venue
description: A looping six-second phone clip shot through the UVU Hall of Flags glass, panning up from the outdoor crowd to track a small fast white object across the sky. Posted by 0HOUR with a caption claiming it shows someone running.

title: Governor Cox On The Clothing Change, Subtitled Duplicate Capture
description: A 23-second subtitled capture of the same Utah press-conference answer in which Governor Spencer Cox describes the suspect changing clothing on the roof and being arrested in the outfit worn before the shooting.

title: Twenty-Nine-Minute Commentary Round-Up
description: A 29-minute reaction video in which a YouTube host assembles other creators' claims about the case, including Google Trends search-pattern arguments, and repeatedly says he does not know what happened.

title: Four Open Questions for the FBI - Slide Presentation
description: An eleven-minute slide presentation setting out four documented threads - a campus security centre, search records, the N1098L flight profile, and drone sightings - as questions for the FBI rather than conclusions.

title: Four Questions Presentation - High-Quality Render
description: The higher-quality render of the eleven-minute slide presentation on the campus security centre, the N1098L flight profile, and the drone-sighting question, with identical narration to the other copy.

title: FINAL CIA Drones: The N1098L Loop and the Questions For the FBI
description: A 14-minute narrated screen-share walking through the UVU national-security centre, Israel-side search clusters, and the N1098L flight profile, ending in a list of questions put to the FBI.

title: Full Drone Cut, 27 October 2025: The Working Copy of the N1098L Walkthrough
description: The dated working copy of the 14-minute N1098L screen-share, byte-identical in transcript to the final cut and useful mainly for establishing when the analysis was assembled.

title: Project Constitution - The Utah State Intelligence Centre Question
description: A 53-second piece to camera on Utah State University's Center for Anticipatory Intelligence, its founders' agency backgrounds, and the single semester Tyler Robinson spent at USU in 2021.

title: RAW CIA Drones: The Four-Node Summary Slide
description: A single static diagram summarising the N1098L thread across four boxes - the UVU national-security centre, Israel-side searches, the September 10 timeline, and the aircraft - carrying its own no-implication disclaimers.

title: The Alibi Clip and the Carpet Comparison
description: Fourteen silent seconds of office CCTV timestamped 09:17 on September 9, 2025, reposted with a claim that the interior finishes match Fort Huachuca. The claim is recorded; it is not adopted.

title: The KSL Interview Where A Witness Describes A Neck Wound And Cheering
description: A 53-second KSL TV field interview in which a young witness describes hearing one loud pop, seeing the shot pass through Kirk's neck from his own left, and a group at the top of the area cheering.

title: The Witness Who Looked For a Crowd Shooter and Saw None
description: A re-cut broadcast interview: the witness gives the heart description, then says he stayed up looking for anyone being set upon in the crowd and saw nothing. The reposter's point-blank headline is not supported by the clip.

title: An On-Camera Witness Account Cut Short
description: An 18-second compilation pairing handheld footage of a young volunteer being stopped mid-account with Fox News segments introducing Cooper Brown as an event volunteer who was feet away from Charlie Kirk.

title: Split-Screen Study of a Guard's Hands
description: A two-minute split-screen edit that loops the seconds after the shot at UVU and puts a red arrow on a kneeling guard's wrist and hands; it is an argument built out of footage, not raw footage.

title: Skyler Baird Answers The Allegations, At Length
description: A 13:53 package pairing a presenter's list of suspicions about witness Skyler Baird with a long split-screen interview in which Baird answers each one directly, in his own words.

title: The "Truman Show" Bubble Around Trump
description: Former NCTC director Joe Kent says a 'Truman Show' echo chamber — Israeli access to Trump's inner circle plus coordinated media repetition — moved the U.S. red line on Iran. Attributed public statements, not proven fact.

title: Charlie Kirk's Handler (Reference)
description: A 26-second clip circulated in July 2026 in which the speaker — identified by the posters as Turning Point COO Tyler Bowyer — describes Mikey McCoy as Charlie Kirk's 'assistant and handler.' This page records only that the word was used on stage by that speaker; it makes no claim of its own about what the word means.

title: Messages & Threats
description: Every reported message Charlie Kirk sent or received in the weeks before September 10, 2025 — one page per message, with its source, its channel, and its verification status.

title: Laurie Cardoza-Moore's Message to Charlie Kirk
description: A screenshot circulated on X shows a long religious rebuke reportedly sent to Charlie Kirk by Christian Zionist activist Laurie Cardoza-Moore days before September 10, 2025. Full text, context, and the case against reading it as a threat.

title: The September 8 Donor Group Chat
description: The nine-person group chat from September 8, 2025 in which Charlie Kirk reportedly wrote about losing donors over Tucker Carlson and leaving the pro-Israel cause — the only message set with published screenshots and an on-the-record TPUSA confirmation.

title: September 9 — "They Are Going To Kill Me"
description: On the day before he died, Charlie Kirk reportedly told at least three people he believed he was about to be killed. No screenshot of those messages has ever been published. What is claimed, by whom, and what is missing.

title: Seth Dillon's Text — "A Cost"
description: Carrie Prejean Boller published a screenshot of a text she attributes to Seth Dillon: Charlie Kirk never said he was bullied or threatened, only that saying certain things would come at a cost. The screenshot and the claim built on it are not the same thing.

title: The Message to Andrew Kolvet
description: TPUSA spokesman Andrew Kolvet is reported to have received a message from Charlie Kirk reading "They will kill me." What Kolvet has confirmed, what he has not, and why he is the most important witness in this section.

title: The Message to Dan Flood
description: Charlie Kirk's head of security is reported to have been told, the night before the assassination, that Kirk expected to be "executed tomorrow." Why a warning to the security chief is different from a warning to a friend.

title: Frank Turek's Text and Email
description: Christian apologist Frank Turek, a mentor to Charlie Kirk, has said publicly that Kirk texted him "I know they want me dead" and emailed him the same warning weeks earlier. The strongest first-person account in this section.

title: Harrison Smith's Account
description: Infowars host Harrison Smith went public saying Charlie Kirk told him days before the assassination that he feared being taken out over Israel. His report is one origin point for the widely circulated August 2025 quotes.

title: "If I Go Against Israel, I Think They Will Kill Me"
description: The most widely circulated quote attributed to Charlie Kirk, reportedly said to a friend on August 13, 2025 — a month before his death. Every recorded variant, every cited source, and why no first-hand recording has ever surfaced.

title: "Wiped Out At Any Time" — The Long-Running Premonition
description: A message attributed to Charlie Kirk describes a decade-long sense that he might be killed at any time, unrelated to any specific threat. It reframes the 2025 messages as an escalation rather than a beginning.

title: Signal and Telegram, Not iMessage
description: Investigation notes state Charlie Kirk sent the threat messages over Signal and Telegram rather than iMessage. That single technical detail reconciles the contradiction between the witnesses and the denial — and decides what can ever be recovered.

title: Erika Kirk's Denial
description: On Glenn Beck's show, Erika Kirk said Charlie was not messaging people the day before saying "they're going to kill me," and that she had his phone. Several named figures describe otherwise. Both accounts, fairly stated.

title: UVU: "He Wants Us To Get A Message To Charlie Kirk"
description: A GRAMA-released email sent through the UVU police chief's chain on September 9, 2025 asked that a message be passed to Charlie Kirk. Every identifying detail is redacted, and whether it was ever delivered is undocumented.

title: Threats to Other Commentators After the Assassination
description: Megyn Kelly, Tucker Carlson, Candace Owens, and Ian Carroll have all publicly described threats in the period after September 10, 2025. What each has said, and what can and cannot be concluded from the pattern.

title: The "Make You Disappear" Remark
description: In a 2024 on-camera interview, Mike Huckabee asked Candace Owens whether she worried that opponents would "make you disappear." The clip resurfaced after the assassination. What was actually said, and why the framing is contested.

title: Candace Owens' Threat Claims
description: Candace Owens has publicly alleged a foreign plot against her own life and a foreign role in Charlie Kirk's death. The most serious and least corroborated set of claims in this section, recorded with the caution it requires.

title: Laurie Cardoza-Moore
description: Laurie Cardoza-Moore is a Christian Zionist activist named in the investigation because a screenshot circulated on X shows a long rebuke reportedly sent to Charlie Kirk days before his death. Context, not accusation.

title: Consciousness Control
description: Consciousness-control claims relevant to the Charlie Kirk case — Havana Syndrome, Voice of God / V2K, directed energy, brain-to-brain research, and why intelligence services would want shooters who look 'crazy.'

title: Havana Syndrome
description: Havana Syndrome — anomalous health incidents, pulsed RF findings vs IC denial, Voice of God / V2K overlap, X whistleblower discourse, and why the 'crazy person' cover matters.

title: Directed Energy Weapons
description: Directed energy weapons — lasers, HPM, ADS, pulsed RF, Voice of God / V2K overlap — what is fielded vs alleged, and why DEW discourse maps to 'crazy shooter' covers.

title: Covert Communications
description: Covert communications tradecraft vs implant/nanotech claims — and how invisible channels create 'crazy lone shooter' covers without exotic physics.

title: Brain-to-Brain Communications
description: Brain-to-brain interfaces — peer-reviewed lab limits vs alleged operational IC systems, X discourse, and the political-shooter cover problem.

title: Communication by Consciousness
description: Claims of consciousness-level communication — Stargate remote viewing, pure telepathy vs electronic synthetic telepathy, and why IC interest does not equal proven UVU use.

title: CIA, DARPA and DEW Mind Control
sidebar_label: CIA, DARPA and DEW Mind Control
description: A 23-minute July 2026 compilation arguing CIA and DARPA involvement in Havana Syndrome — with the underlying patents, the 1994 Air Force New World Vistas passage, DARPA's N3 program, and a line-by-line separation of what is documented from what is asserted.

title: Were Charlie's Podcasts Deleted?
description: Direct check of whether the episodes Charlie Kirk himself hosted before September 10, 2025 are still on Spotify and Apple Podcasts today — measured against the show's own master RSS feed.

title: Apple Podcasts: Charlie's 752 Episodes Removed
description: Apple Podcasts listed 752 episodes of The Charlie Kirk Show in August 2025. Every episode published in August 2025 or earlier is now gone from the platform under its original date.

title: Every Apple Podcasts Episode Removed: The Full List of 1,793
description: The complete, episode-by-episode list of the 1,793 Charlie Kirk Show episodes that Wayback Machine captures show were on Apple Podcasts and that are gone from the live Apple catalog as of July 31, 2026. Every one was published while Charlie Kirk was alive.

title: Roof
description: The Losee Center roof at UVU on September 10, 2025 — the alleged firing position, run and military crawl, black clothing vs jeans, screwdriver and helicopter disputes, muzzle-flash claims, and identity questions.

title: Roof Timeline — September 10, 2025
description: Every roof event in order — the morning approach, the railing crossing, the alleged assembly point and screwdriver, the run and prone position, the drop to the grass, and the scene processing and footage releases afterward.

title: The Tactical Roof Run
description: Frame measurement of the running figure on the Losee Center roof — where he enters the frame relative to the alleged screwdriver drop point, the 10-11 running steps between marked points, and the lateral crawl into position.

title: The Screwdriver and the Crime-Scene Tape
description: Reported testimony that a screwdriver was recovered 15-20 feet past the Losee Center roof railing and protected with yellow crime-scene tape, set against helicopter footage said to show no tape at the railing.

title: Line of Sight Behind the Roof Lip
sidebar_label: Line of Sight Behind the Roof Lip
description: If the shooter lay flat behind a five-inch roof lip set back from the edge, how did he see down into the UVU courtyard? The geometry question raised against the prone firing position on the Losee Center roof.

title: Military Lateral Crawl
description: Citizen claims that the Losee Center roof figure used a dedicated military lateral crawl into prone position — Candace Owens footage, training inferences, and counter-arguments.

title: Black Clothing vs Jeans

title: Provo (KPVU) — April 2024 to September 2025

title: Wichita (KICT) — November 2022 to August 2025
description: Egyptian-registered Falcon 7X jets visited Wichita, Kansas repeatedly between 2022 and 2025 — the Air Capital of the World, home to an FAA Part 145 Dassault Falcon service centre. The overlap counts and the audit disagree about most of these dates.

title: Wilmington (KILG) — November 2022 to October 2025
description: The most-visited airport in the entire Egyptian fleet record — and it appears on the outbound leg only, every single time, for three years. Wilmington, Delaware is a customs stop that the overlap counts score as a destination.

title: St. Louis (KSTL / KCPS) — December 2022 to February 2025
description: Missouri is one of the five states in the shadowing clustering. St. Louis is where the 2023 TPUSA Faith tour launch produces the closest documented Kirk-side pairing — and where two airports fifteen minutes apart get counted as two visits.

title: Minot (KMOT) — April to September 2025
description: Every Provo-bound Egyptian jet in 2025 entered the United States at Minot, North Dakota — a small northern field beside a nuclear-mission Air Force base. This is where customs happened, not Provo, and nobody has requested the records.

title: Everyone Named In The Following-Planes Material

title: Paris–Le Bourget (LFPB) — October 2022 to October 2025
description: Every Egyptian jet in this investigation staged through Paris-Le Bourget on its way to the United States. Eighteen recorded stops, one overnight each, and never once on the way home. It is the most-repeated node in the whole dataset and it is in a country nobody has alleged anything about.

title: Goose Bay (CYYR) — May 2023 to September 2025
description: The two Egyptian Gulfstreams crossed the Atlantic through a Canadian Forces base in Labrador; the three Falcons never did. It is the cleanest aircraft-type explanation in the whole dataset — and it is where SU-BND left North America three days after the assassination.

title: Williston (KXWA) — 23 April 2024
description: A single arrival, and the one that sets the pattern: in 2024 the Utah-bound Egyptian jet entered the United States at Williston, North Dakota. In 2025 it was Minot, four times. Every Provo rotation across two years came in through North Dakota.

title: Detroit (KDTW) — February and March 2025

title: 29 April 2025 — Lincoln, NE
description: Row EXTRA-007: amplifier claim that Tyler Robinson's apartment address was Google-searched in Hebrew from an Egyptian jet parked in Lincoln, Nebraska on 29 April 2025. Not on the Owens sheet. No tail number in the posts. Not a 74th row of the 73.

title: Erika Kirk's flights — what the X posts actually claim
description: The first dedicated page for Erika Kirk's alleged flights in the following-pattern: what X accounts said, which tail they pointed at, her own on-camera invitation to check the logs, the reported FlightRadar24 removal, and why her itinerary is the weak side of every overlap tally. Researcher claims, not a finding.

title: The claim that the planes tracked Erika, not Charlie
description: On 17 November 2025, X accounts amplifying Candace Owens alleged that Egyptian-registered jets had been overlapping Erika Kirk's travel, not Charlie Kirk's. 68, 70, 72, and 73 are the numbers they posted. Tracker tallies, not a finding.

title: The overseas-overlap claim — Erika Kirk and the Egyptian jets abroad
description: X accounts alleged that SU-BTT and SU-BND overlapped Erika Kirk on international legs, not only at US fields. No dated overseas pairing has been published except a spreadsheet cell that put her 'potentially in Giza.' Researcher claims, not a finding.

title: Erika Kirk on 10 September 2025 — competing flight claims
description: X accounts do not agree on where Erika Kirk was on 10 September 2025. She has been reported as staying in Arizona; as flying into Provo that afternoon on N102DZ; and, in a later Baron Coleman thread, as possibly arriving at 10:06 a.m. on N560TW. All three cannot be right. None is a finding of wrongdoing.

title: How the spreadsheet placed Erika Kirk — Instagram, not flight logs
description: The overlap sheet's Erika Location column is mostly US states, sometimes two states at once, with Notes that read 'Instagram confirms presence.' That is the substitute for her unpublished flight logs. A social-media post is not a timestamp and not a coordinate.

title: What the compilers counted as an 'overlap'
description: Liz Wheeler's December 2025 posts: the overlap spreadsheet counted an Egyptian jet within 50–100 miles and ±3 days of a claimed Erika Kirk location. Same airport, same day, she said, dwindles to one — Utah on 10 September, after the shooting, jets already down.

title: Erika Kirk's invitation to check her flight logs
description: Erika Kirk on camera invited the public to go through her flight log, denied being on an Egyptian plane, and offered a hospital photo for at least one contested date. X accounts then alleged the N102DZ history she pointed at had already been removed from FlightRadar24.

title: X accounts that posted about Erika Kirk's flights
description: Named X accounts whose posts are the source layer for the Erika-Kirk flight cluster — amplifiers of the 68/73 tally, the FlightRadar24-erasure claim, Liz Wheeler's window critique, Kanekoa's audit, and the Sept 10 whereabouts threads. Quoted as speakers, not as findings.

title: Getting The Data — How This Investigation Checks The Flight Claims Itself
description: The four passes this investigation uses to check the following-planes claim against primary flight data: free open sources, commercial APIs, government records, and captures of the tracking websites themselves — including what each one found and what it could not.

title: Open Flight Data — Checking The Following Claim Against Primary ADS-B
description: The free, open flight-tracking sources: which have historical data and which only have live positions, how to call them, and what happened when we ran every claimed overlap date in this investigation through primary ADS-B traces.

title: The Volunteer Network — The Open ADS-B System That Runs Parallel To The Paid Trackers
description: How the community ADS-B system actually collects, shares and archives flight data; why it shows aircraft the commercial trackers are asked to hide; and the geographic sweep this investigation built on top of it to ask what was near every Charlie Kirk event, rather than asking about tails somebody already named.

title: Commercial Flight-Data APIs — What They Would Settle, And What They Cost
description: Flightradar24, FlightAware and ADS-B Exchange hold the deep flight history the free networks do not — including the whole 2022 window this investigation cannot otherwise reach. What each would answer, what it costs, and what their terms allow us to publish.

title: Government Flight Records — What Is Downloadable And What Must Be Requested
description: The government sources for aircraft ownership, airport operations and ramp records — what downloads freely today, what has to be asked for under FOIA or state public-records law, and the fact that the five Egyptian tails at the centre of this case appear in none of it.

title: Capturing The Tracking Websites — And Proving What They Used To Show
description: Driving a real browser at the flight-tracking sites to record what the public actually sees, compare it against Internet Archive snapshots, and document honestly where data that was once public is no longer retrievable.

title: Aircraft Costs — What Every Plane in This Case Costs New
description: Every aircraft in the Charlie Kirk investigation priced as if bought new today — 33 airframes, roughly $1.10 billion combined. FAA-confirmed types, current manufacturer list prices, and a named in-production comparable for every out-of-production aircraft.

title: TPUSA Aircraft — What Turning Point Actually Owned
description: A direct check of the FAA aircraft registry for aircraft registered to Turning Point USA or Turning Point Action. The registry returns none. This page documents what the search found, which tails commentary has attached to TPUSA anyway, and who each of those tails is actually registered to.

title: Which Planes Charlie Flew, Which Planes Erika Flew
description: Separating the aircraft record for Charlie Kirk from the aircraft record for Erika Kirk. Charlie's side has a tail number. Erika's side, in 85 spreadsheet rows, has none — the overlap tally never records which aircraft she was on.

title: LASAI Aviation — The Whole Fleet Behind N1098L
description: N1098L is not a lone aircraft. The FAA registry shows LASAI Aviation LLC and LASAI Aviation II LLC operating a fleet of fifteen aircraft from Manassas and Reston, Virginia — three Bombardier Globals, two Challenger 650s, and six King Air 350s. This is the full list.

title: N155TV — KSL Chopper 5 Over UVU
description: N155TV is KSL Chopper 5, a 1990 Bell 206L-3 LongRanger III. FlightRadar24 playback shows it orbiting the Utah Valley University campus on the afternoon of September 10, 2025 — the aircraft behind the 'the screwdriver wasn't on the roof' claim.

title: N708JH — The DOJ Gulfstream
description: N708JH is a 2019 Gulfstream G550 registered directly to the United States Government, Department of Justice. It appears in the Charlie Kirk investigation through a claim about a tracking block, and the registry confirms the one part of that claim that can be checked.

title: N885LS — The Las Vegas Sands BBJ
description: N885LS is a 2001 Boeing 737-7EL business jet registered to Las Vegas Sands Corp. It is associated in case notes with the May 27, 2025 Las Vegas entry for Air Force Two tail 99-0004, and it is the second-most expensive aircraft in this investigation.

title: Flight Data Recovery — What Was Erased, What Was Not, And What We Got Back
description: This investigation assumed the flight records had been erased and went looking for backups across all sixteen aircraft. No tracking site was found to have removed anything — every page still loads, and the 403s were robot blocks. What the sweep did produce is a large body of flight data nobody here had held before, including the first primary tracks behind the alleged following-flights.

title: What A 403 Actually Means
description: This site published that N102DZ's FlightRadar24 page was a documented removal because the URL returns HTTP 403. It was not. Five unrelated control aircraft got the identical 403 from the identical script, and in a real browser all twenty pages load HTTP 200. This is the method that caught it, written so any reader can run it.

title: Per-Aircraft Recovery Status
description: One row and one section per aircraft: what every flight-data source still holds for that tail, what it does not, how far back each archive reaches, and how many flight rows were recovered from archived pages. Across sixteen aircraft and five tracking sites, no page was found removed.

title: Overlap Recovery — Every Alleged Following-Flight, Tested
description: The 73-overlap spreadsheet claims an Egyptian government jet was in a specific American city on a specific date. All 69 testable aircraft-and-date pairs were pulled against both free daily ADS-B archives. Twenty-three now have a primary track: twenty-one put the aircraft in the alleged country, two put it on the wrong continent. Thirty-nine have nothing in the window at all.

title: Investigating Deleted Flights — Status, Coverage, and What We Recovered
description: The working status of the effort to recover flight records that went missing from the public trackers: what percentage of the data we now hold and against which denominator, which archive lane produced it, the four Egyptian ground presences the union of both routes returns, and the defects found in our own code and published against ourselves.

description: Entry point to the two picture walls of the aircraft investigation — 227 photographs and 30 videos, each on one scrolling page at true aspect ratio, each tile linking to its own evidence page.

title: Every Plane Photo In One Place
description: Every photograph in the aircraft investigation on one page — 227 images in two columns at their real aspect ratio, two sentences under each, every tile clicking through to its own evidence page.

title: Every Plane Video In One Place
description: Every video in the aircraft and drone investigation on one page — 30 clips playable in place at true aspect ratio, with a three-sentence flight-data interlude after every fourth clip.

title: AI Defense Attorney — What We Would Do Differently
description: A theoretical exercise: what an idealised defense attorney would do in State of Utah v. Tyler Robinson that does not appear on the public record — twenty-one differences, the stage each belongs to, and the witness or discovery target for each.

title: Legal Documents — State v. Robinson
description: Primary-source filings in State of Utah v. Tyler Robinson, case 251403576 — 374 documents held against an 867-entry docket, the transcripts and exhibits, the remaining gaps, and the priced routes to close them.

title: Score Card — The Ideal Defense Attorney
description: The legal courtroom score card: twenty-one areas where an idealised defense attorney might act differently, and a structured way for a reader to decide, area by area, whether they think there is a problem.

title: Sept 10 Travel Routes and Timing — UVU, Dairy Queen, Panguitch
description: A citizen mapping walkthrough of Tyler Robinson's alleged September 10, 2025 locations — St. George, UVU, a nearby Dairy Queen, and Cowboy's Smokehouse in Panguitch — measuring the drive legs and asking which arrangement of the day is physically possible.

title: Panguitch Restaurant Reportedly Told Not to Answer Further Questions (Claims)
description: Ian Wendt says the owner of Cowboy's Smokehouse in Panguitch told him a waiter saw Tyler Robinson, that they gave everything to the FBI, and that the FBI told them not to say any more or answer further questions.

title: Hebrew-Language Searches and the Egyptian Jets (Claims)
description: Stew Peters' August 5 2026 segment claiming Hebrew-language Google searches for Erika Kirk's maiden name, Tyler Robinson's address, the Losee Center and Orem SIM cards appear on the same dates an Egyptian military aircraft was on the ground in the United States — with the limits of that inference stated.

title: A Crowd-Angle Excerpt Posted As Two Separate Holes
description: A 4.6-second excerpt of the moment of the shot, filmed from inside the crowd beside the tent and screen-recorded off a phone, posted with the claim that two separate holes are visible — one in the neck and one in the shirt.

title: The Command-Center Truck Across From UVU (Claims)
description: A citizen journalist says the white box truck parked across from UVU on September 10, 2025 carries the same roof-mounted communications antenna and climate-control unit as a special-operations SWAT vehicle photographed in St George — the comparison, and why matching roof silhouettes cannot identify a vehicle.

title: The Fed Narrative
description: The ten points of the official federal and state account of the Charlie Kirk assassination, each mapped to what citizen investigators say contradicts it — with the ordinary innocent explanation given alongside every objection.

title: Score Cards
description: Tools that let a reader measure the case themselves — score a commentator against the ten points of the federal account, or score the defense against what an ideal capital attorney would have filed.

title: Chains of Reasoning
description: Each chain is a numbered sequence of facts that together support one conclusion — stated as a chain, with the strength of every link marked and the strongest objection printed at the bottom.

title: Fed Claim: He Turned Himself In
description: The federal and state account says Tyler Robinson voluntarily surrendered around 10 PM on September 11, 2025. Defense filings, a booking sheet, and a GRAMA hearing point to a much earlier custody time.

title: Fed Claim: The Discord Confession
description: The claim that Tyler Robinson confessed on Discord around 8 PM on September 11, 2025 — and the custody record that would make it impossible for him to have typed it.

title: Fed Claim: A .30-06 Round Killed Him
description: The official cause of death is a single .30-06 rifle round to the neck. Citizen investigators reject it on energy, trajectory, acoustics, and wound grounds, and conclude an explosive device.

title: Fed Claim: DNA and the Grandfather's Rifle
description: The state says DNA consistent with Tyler Robinson was on the trigger, the casings, the towel and the screwdriver. Investigators ask about transfer, custody, fingerprints, and the sequence in which the rifle was found.

title: Fed Claim: Engraved Casings Show the Motive
description: Engraved ammunition and a claimed ideological motive became the emotional core of the official story. The engravings are internet meme text, and the suspect's own reported texts call them 'mostly a big meme'.

title: Fed Claim: The Rooftop Figure Is Robinson
description: The FBI released rooftop and stairwell imagery as the shooter. Investigators point to clothing conflicts, a trained movement profile, an absent muzzle flash, and a backpack that does not fit a full-length rifle.

title: Fed Claim: His Family Turned Him In
description: The official story has a relative reaching a family friend who called police. Reporting and family-adjacent accounts describe a former deputy and Boy Scout leader persuading Robinson to come in, and a father who did not identify him.

title: Fed Claim: The 33-Hour Manhunt
description: The published timeline runs 33 hours from shot to capture. The custody documents compress it, and the Panguitch restaurant account would place Robinson 209 miles away during the manhunt texts.

title: Fed Claim: He Acted Alone
description: The lone-gunman finding arrived within days. It sits alongside the FBI's own statement that it was investigating twenty or more Discord users, and alongside a halted federal review of foreign ties.

title: Fed Claim: Nothing Was Hidden
description: The official posture is a transparent, by-the-book investigation. The record shows a courtyard paved within days, a sealed autopsy, missing bodycam and CCTV, deleted witness video, gag orders, and erased flight data.

title: Fed Narrative Score Card
description: Score any commentator, outlet, or official against the ten points of the federal account. Ten questions, a scoring key, and a worked example — so a reader can measure who is repeating talking points and who is checking them.

title: Defense Attorney Score Card
description: Score the defense in State of Utah v. Tyler Robinson against what an ideal capital defense team would have done — twelve motions, each with the record it would have opened.

title: Chain: Why It Was Not a .30-06
description: A step-by-step chain of reasoning from the physical record to the conclusion that a single .30-06 rifle round fired from the Losee Center roof did not kill Charlie Kirk.

title: Chain: Why a Shaped Charge in the Microphone
description: A step-by-step chain of reasoning from the video, the audio, the burnt object, the hardware, and the destroyed scene to the conclusion that an explosive device at the lapel microphone killed Charlie Kirk.

title: Chain: The Following Planes, and Deducing the Country
description: A step-by-step chain from primary ADS-B position data to the argument that the aircraft near Charlie Kirk's events were intelligence platforms — and an honest account of how far the inference to Israel actually reaches.

title: Chain: He Could Not Have Sent the Discord Confession
description: A step-by-step chain from the Bates-stamped Miranda video, the booking sheet, and Discord's own timestamps to the conclusion that Tyler Robinson could not have typed the 'It was me at UVU' message.

title: Chain: Panguitch Breaks the Evening Manhunt
description: A step-by-step chain from restaurant-staff identification
column17: and road miles to the conclusion that the state's evening-of-September-10 Orem-area timeline cannot share a clock with Cowboy's Smokehouse in Panguitch.

title: Chain: The Rooftop Figure Is Not Identified as Robinson
description: A step-by-step chain from clothing conflicts, backpack size, movement profile, absent muzzle flash, uncalled eyewitnesses, and a BOLO released after the custody time to the conclusion that the Losee Center rooftop figure has not been identified as Tyler Robinson.

title: Chain: He Did Not Turn Himself In at 10 PM
description: A step-by-step chain from the Miranda video, the booking sheet, the missing bodycam and lobby CCTV, and the SBI transport timing to the conclusion that the public 'he turned himself in around 10 PM' story does not survive the state's own documents.

title: Chain: The Scene That Would Have Answered It Was Destroyed
description: A step-by-step chain from the paved courtyard, hauled dirt, destroyed SUV, empty camera systems, pulled SD cards, sealed autopsy, and deleted witness video to the conclusion that the official 'nothing was hidden' posture is incompatible with the pattern of what is gone.

title: Chain: The Lone-Gunman Finding Cannot Absorb the Intelligence Indicators
description: A step-by-step chain from Patel's 20-plus Discord users, a halted NCTC foreign-ties review, a US Army HADES overflight, foreign-registered jets at Provo, and professional-hit indicators to the conclusion that 'he acted alone' is a posture, not a shown result.

title: Chain: DNA on a Household Rifle Does Not Prove a Shot
description: A step-by-step chain from household-rifle DNA, no reported print match, no reported GSR, a contested discovery sequence, an inconclusive ATF fragment, and a screwdriver aerial-footage dispute to the conclusion that the state's strongest evidence still does not establish that Tyler Robinson fired a shot at UVU.

title: Getting The Recovered Flight Data Into Evidence
description: Citizen-recovered flight data is worthless in a courtroom until it is authenticated. This is the Rule 901 and 902(13)/(14) route, the custodian and expert witnesses who make it stick, and why the control-aircraft discipline — including a published retraction — is the authentication. Theoretical exercise.

title: T6 — Aircraft Supported The Operation, And Associated Ground Vehicles Were Rented
description: The thesis with the best evidence-handling behind it and the hardest ceiling above it: 1,831 aircraft-days of recovered primary ADS-B data prove presence and nothing else, while the reachable half — rental agreements, fuel tickets, ramp logs, telematics — was never demanded from anyone before the retention windows shut. Theoretical exercise.

title: File The Alternative-Perpetrator Notice First
description: Every foreign-nexus subpoena in this case depends on one procedural step that has to come first: putting an alternative-perpetrator defense formally before the court. Theoretical exercise.

title: Subpoena The AV Procurement Chain — Purchase Orders To Delivery
description: The documentary half of the device question: a subpoena duces tecum rider for the purchase orders, quotations, invoices, packing lists, bills of lading, receiving signatures, serial-number assignments and custody records behind the audio equipment used on September 10, 2025. Theoretical exercise.

title: Move To Exclude Any Revived Lead-Comparison Evidence
description: The ATF comparison came back inconclusive and the fragment moved to a federal lab. A defense attorney would pre-emptively challenge any revival of comparative bullet-lead analysis. Theoretical exercise.

title: Retain A Blast Expert And An Acoustics Expert
description: No explosives expert and no acoustician appears on the public record in this case. A defense attorney testing an alternative mechanism of death would retain both. Theoretical exercise.

title: Establish Whether A Bomb Sweep Was Ever Run
description: Explosive-detection dogs and EOD teams either swept the UVU site or they did not, and either found something or did not. A defense attorney would establish which. Theoretical exercise.

title: Convert The Brady Demands Into A Sanctions Motion
description: Discovery demands have been outstanding against federal agencies since 2025. A defense attorney would stop asking and start moving for sanctions. Theoretical exercise.

title: Demand The Full Campus Camera Inventory And The Retention Record
description: The State produced sixteen Bates pages of UVU surveillance. A defense asks the other question: out of how many cameras? A Rule 14 subpoena for the campus camera inventory, the retention schedule and the machine-generated export log. Theoretical exercise.

title: Case Stage Map — Which Files Track Which Stage
description: How the court directories on this site map onto the stages of State of Utah v. Tyler Robinson, and what each status value in this section actually means.

title: What Was Collected, What Was Analysed, And What Happened To The Difference
description: A tower dump was taken from three national carriers in this case and the return describes it in five words. An AI defense attorney would move for the collection inventory, the analysis log, the filter criteria and the disposition of everything filtered out. Theoretical exercise.

title: Move To Suppress The Attributed Confession
description: A defense exhibit puts the rights warning at 6:25 PM on September 11; the messages attributed to the defendant appear around 7:57 PM. A defense attorney would move to suppress. Theoretical exercise.

title: Move To Suppress The Crime-Scene Evidence
description: Twenty-five search warrants are public in State v. Robinson. Not one of them covers the UVU crime scene itself. An AI defense attorney would move under Rule 12 to suppress everything taken from the four scenes, and in the alternative to compel the complete warrant inventory and every return. Theoretical exercise.

title: Demand The Detention And Release Record — And The Arrival Order
description: A records-only defense instrument: the field-contact, detention, booking, Miranda, property-inventory and report-of-investigation paperwork for every stop in the operational period, plus the four machine-generated sources that fix which agency reached each address first. Theoretical exercise.

title: T4 — US Military Intelligence Acted On Foreign Direction, And It Reaches The Hardware
sidebar_label: T4 — Direction Of US Military Intelligence
description: Thesis 4 of the AI defense attorney exercise: that elements of US military intelligence acted at foreign direction, and that the direction reaches the hardware — the ordering, funding and delivery of the audio equipment, and who was present. Split into a reachable documentary half and an unreachable half. Theoretical exercise.

title: Subpoena The Dispatch And CAD Record
description: The cheapest instrument in the case: a Rule 14 subpoena duces tecum for the complete CAD incident record, the radio log, the look-out issuance record and the licence-plate-reader query log for September 10, 2025 — machine-generated, contemporaneous, and nobody wrote it for litigation. Theoretical exercise.

title: Demand The State's Own Exhibits — And The Six Numbers Missing From Its List
description: A motion to compel native, Bates-numbered production of every preliminary-hearing exhibit, a demand for the clerk's list of what was actually received, and the question of what happened to exhibits 17, 18, 26, 27, 28 and 29. Theoretical exercise.

title: Move For Court-Ordered Explosive Residue Testing
description: The first motion an AI defense attorney would file: a court order compelling GC-MS and IMS explosive-residue testing of every item retained from September 10, 2025, and production of the full lab request log. Theoretical exercise.

title: Whether To Call The Victim's Widow And Inner Circle
description: A theoretical exercise on whether an idealised defense attorney would call the victim's widow or inner circle, what could lawfully be asked, and why the answer is probably no.

title: Retain A Point-Cloud Expert — The State's Own 3D Scan Of The Scene
description: 660 gigabytes of raw FARO 3D laser-scan data of the scene reached the defense on July 20, 2026. An AI defense attorney would fund an expert to read it, demand the scan metadata and registration report, and date every scan position against the day the courtyard was resurfaced. Theoretical exercise.

title: Put FBI Case Agents On The Stand
description: Exactly one FBI witness testified at the preliminary hearing, and she was a DNA examiner called by the defense. A defense attorney would subpoena the agents who ran the scene. Theoretical exercise.

title: Subpoena The FBO And Ground-Handling Records
description: An ADS-B trace proves an aircraft was there. The fuel ticket, the ramp log, the badge swipe and the handling invoice prove what it did and sometimes who was aboard. The paper a physical aircraft generates on the ground, and how a defense would subpoena it. Theoretical exercise.

title: T2 — Federal Handling Of The Scene And Of Discovery Has Kept Material Out Of The Case
description: A discovery and spoliation thesis in State of Utah v. Tyler Robinson: the death scene was processed by a federal agency and then excavated, evidence routed federally first, nine DNA samples entirely consumed, three autopsy fragments unaccounted for, and material the FBI and ATF have declined to produce. Theoretical exercise.

title: The Foreign-Carrier Route — And Why A Court Would Likely Refuse It
description: A state trial court cannot subpoena a foreign telecom, and a criminal defendant cannot compel an MLAT request. We would serve the demand anyway, docket the refusal as evidence, and then answer the same question from the domestic tower dumps the State already holds. Theoretical exercise.

title: T3 — A Foreign State Decided On The Assassination And People Here Were Told Beforehand
description: The contention that the decision to kill Charlie Kirk originated outside the United States and that there was advance notification inside it — built in the order a court would require, starting with the alternative-perpetrator notice and the one named official who has already spoken. Theoretical exercise.

title: Foreign-Registered Handsets On Campus
description: Thesis T7. A tower dump was taken from three national carriers and the return describes it in eight words. The discovery corpus holds at least 25,253 location records. Somebody decided which subset mattered. An AI defense attorney would demand that decision. Theoretical exercise.

title: Records Demand On The September 9 Meeting Week
description: A records demand for base access, flight and scheduling documents covering September 8 and 9, 2025 — sought as documents, with no attendee named. Theoretical exercise.

title: Reconsider The Secrecy Posture
description: The defense argued material was exculpatory and then moved to seal it. An AI defense attorney would examine whether secrecy still serves this defendant. Theoretical exercise.

title: Move For The Hearing Audio The Court Already Ordered Released
description: An instrument that asks for something a judge has already ordered released: the redacted audio of the October 24, 2025 sealed hearing, plus certified transcripts of the eight hearings that exist in no certified form outside the court. Theoretical exercise.

title: Subpoena The Hospital And Transport Record
description: The interval between the wound and the pronouncement of death is documented by people who are not police. A defense attorney would subpoena that record. Theoretical exercise.

title: The Frontage Camera Canvass And The Retention Windows That Beat It
description: The neighbourhood video canvass is the most time-critical act a defense investigator ever performs. Consumer and small-business retention windows close in days to weeks. What an AI defense attorney would have served on 12 September 2025, and the one instrument that still works today. Theoretical exercise.

title: Retain An Independent Forensic Pathologist And Cross The Medical Examiner
description: The autopsy entered the preliminary hearing through a case agent rather than the medical examiner. A defense attorney would retain an independent pathologist and cross the examiner directly. Theoretical exercise.

title: Order An Independent Re-Extraction Of The Devices
description: The device evidence was produced through a commercial forensic tool. A defense attorney would have its own examiner re-extract from the original images. Theoretical exercise.

title: T1 — The Mechanism Of Death Was An Explosive, Not A Rifle Round
description: The load-bearing thesis of this section: an AI defense attorney would contend the fatal wound was caused by a shaped charge at chest height, not a .30-06 round from the Losee Center roof — and would prove or disprove it with the cheapest procedure in forensic chemistry. Theoretical exercise.

title: Method — How This Exercise Works
description: The rules this section follows: public record only, an honest counterargument on every page, timing before criticism, no accusations against living people, and a plain statement of what the defense is doing well.

title: Subpoena The Microphone Itself
description: The device at the centre of the alternative theory of death is a specific piece of hardware with a serial number, a supply chain and an AV crew. A defense attorney would subpoena it. Theoretical exercise.

title: Subpoena The Halted Foreign-Nexus Inquiry
description: A sitting intelligence official has said publicly that his foreign-involvement inquiry into Charlie Kirk's death was stopped by the FBI. A defense attorney would subpoena him and the records. Theoretical exercise.

title: AI Defense Attorney — What We Would Do Differently
description: A theoretical exercise: what a defense attorney retained on September 12, 2025 would do in State of Utah v. Tyler Robinson that does not appear on the public record — nine contentions, thirty-seven instruments, the stage each belongs to, and the witness or discovery target for each.

title: Subpoena The Rental Agreements — The Reachable Half Of The Vehicle Question
description: The most reachable instrument in the aircraft-and-ground-vehicles cluster: an ordinary subpoena duces tecum to car rental companies for agreements, driver records, VINs, odometers, tolls and telematics in the September 2025 window. Theoretical exercise.

title: File A Spoliation Motion Over The Altered Crime Scene
description: The courtyard was excavated, paved and reworked within days. A defense attorney would seek spoliation sanctions and an adverse-inference instruction. Theoretical exercise.

title: Force Disclosure Of The Seized Security-Detail Clothing
description: Clothing was reportedly taken from members of Charlie Kirk's protective detail after September 10, 2025. A defense attorney would demand the evidence numbers and every test run on those items. Theoretical exercise.

title: Subpoena The Soil — Who Ordered The Ten-Inch Dig
description: Roughly ten inches of soil left the UVU tent courtyard before the paving crew arrived. A defense attorney would subpoena the work order, the disposal manifest, and the destination. Theoretical exercise.

title: Move To Exclude The State's Experts — No Notice Appears On The Docket
description: A two-part instrument: compel the State's Utah Code 77-17-13 expert notice on a date certain now, and pre-commit a trial motion in limine excluding any expert never noticed and any laboratory report offered through a witness who did not write it. Theoretical exercise.

title: The Day-One Track — What A Defense Retained On September 12, 2025 Would Have Served
description: A dated counterfactual discovery calendar for State of Utah v. Tyler Robinson: what an AI defense attorney retained on September 12, 2025 would have served, on what date, what was still recoverable then, and when each window closed. Theoretical exercise.

title: The Diverted Pursuit — Where The First Hours Of The Investigation Went
description: Appendix A thesis T5. Local police effort on the afternoon of September 10, 2025 was directed toward two private individuals in vehicles, and that direction absorbed the first hours of a capital investigation. A records thesis built entirely on machine-generated timestamps. Theoretical exercise.

title: T8 — A University-Owned Property Near The Site Was Likely Used
description: The most reachable thesis in the appendix: a public institution owns a house on the street the State drew a geofence through, and its occupancy, keying, access-control and utility records are obtainable by subpoena and by GRAMA with no gateway to clear. Theoretical exercise.

title: Subpoena The Organization's Own Records
description: The event, the venue contract, the security arrangements, the AV vendor and the travel were all organised by a private organisation whose records are reachable by ordinary subpoena. Theoretical exercise.

title: Force The Custody File On The Transport SUV
description: The GMC Yukon that carried Charlie Kirk from UVU was reportedly towed, cleaned and put on a resale path. A defense attorney would demand its evidence log, release date and test list. Theoretical exercise.

title: Trial Cursor — Where The Case Is Right Now
description: Where State of Utah v. Tyler Robinson stands as of September 1, 2026: the preliminary hearing is complete, the State has rested, and bind-over oral argument is being heard today. No ruling has issued.

title: Two Tracks Compared — The Counterfactual Against The Visible Record
description: The same twelve months, run twice: what an AI defense attorney retained on September 12, 2025 would have done by each milestone, set against what the public record of State of Utah v. Tyler Robinson actually shows. Theoretical exercise.

title: Subpoena The University For Its Own Property Records
description: The most reachable instrument in the whole appendix: a subpoena duces tecum to Utah Valley University for the occupancy, keying, access-control, work-order, utility, parking and insurance records of the house it owns at 691 W 925 S, Orem. Theoretical exercise.

title: Exculpatory Material Exists And Has Not Been Provided
description: Two halves of one thesis, kept apart on purpose: the campus half is ordinary Brady and spoliation practice against a reachable Utah custodian and is close to a certainty, and the federal half depends on a gateway ruling. Theoretical exercise.

title: People's Analysis
description: One page per person who gives their opinion on what happened to Charlie Kirk — their video, transcript, and argument. Opinions, not findings.
